links.site_note: The AP says he has a basic campaign website and a Facebook page; the URL was not opened here (another pass lists sullivanforsenate.com from The Green Papers).

oneliner.t: Retired Petersburg schoolteacher and former Forest Service worker, unrelated to the senator, who filed for the Senate days before the June 1 deadline. The state tried to disqualify him, the courts restored him, and he finished third in the primary (2.5%); he appears on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. with no party label.

born.note: Age 69 from both AP and his Beacon questionnaire; birthplace only from his own questionnaire answer.

upbringing.t: By his own questionnaire, born in Evergreen Park and raised in Homewood, Illinois, and living in Petersburg since 1980. He worked as a forestry technician (AP: U.S. Forest Service) and then taught elementary and middle school for about 20 years; a local Assembly member who worked with him calls his character 'unimpeachable.' Locals had previously urged him to run for local office. He lists volunteer service as a firefighter, youth coach and music teacher, arts council president, volunteer radio host and member of a Public Safety Advisory Board.

profile.office_years_note: No elected office. The Public Safety Advisory Board role is a self-reported advisory appointment.

career.role: Elementary and middle school teacher (literature, reading, writing)

platform.t: Says tariffs and the Iran war are raising Alaskans' costs; calls housing and health care immediate needs and education a key investment.
Calls the war with Iran 'ill-conceived' and faults the senator for backing it.

Opposes Medicaid work requirements (citing seasonal and subsistence work); says rural health money passed last year does not meet immediate needs; says government should stay out of personal health decisions including abortion.
Backs sustainable resource development, science-based fisheries management and NOAA research; would support the Ambler Road only if it addresses concerns of communities that use the land.
Supports open primaries and ranked-choice voting.

promises_note: No specific campaign promises found beyond the positions above.

said.where: Alaska Beacon voter-guide questionnaire (substitute for unopened campaign site)

record.t: AP also reports his age as 69.
AP describes him as a retired elementary and middle school teacher and quotes a former colleague; length of service not independently confirmed.
AP calls him a former U.S. Forest Service employee.
AP says he has lived in Petersburg 'for decades'; the 1980 date is not independently confirmed.

claims.claim: He followed every filing rule and meets the constitutional requirements to run.

said.where: letter to the lieutenant governor and interview (KFSK/Alaska Public Media)

record.t: A Superior Court judge ruled the 'good faith' standard used to disqualify him had no basis in the Constitution, state law or regulation, and the Alaska Supreme Court affirmed on June 29 and ordered him onto the ballot.

claims.claim: He is not working with Peltola or Democrats.

record.t: No document shows coordination: the elections director cited none and a Superior Court judge ruled the Division of Elections’ new "good faith" test had no basis in law (he did not rule on coordination). His launch consultant, Amber Lee, has worked for Democrats and publicly backed Peltola, and is an unpaid board member of the 907 Initiative, which ran anti-Sen. Sullivan ads; an FEC complaint over that link, filed by Americans for Public Trust, is pending and cannot be decided while the FEC lacks a quorum.

claims.claim: His blue-and-gold branding is based on the Alaska flag.

record.t: The NRSC says his logo nearly copies the senator's trademarked branding, and the elections director cited website similarity. Intent is not checkable.

claims.claim: The Trump administration denied Alaska's request for higher reimbursement after Typhoon Halong.

aipac_endorse.t: No AIPAC endorsement found; not listed on Track AIPAC's candidates page (as of 2026-10-08).

aipac_pac.note: 2026 cycle: his FEC summary shows $0 from PACs or other committees.

fec.src_note: self = $10,400 in candidate loans. Debts of $14,780.41 owed by the committee are not itemized on the summary page.
fec.outside_note: No independent expenditures for or against him were found. The 907 Initiative (>$1M in ads featuring the incumbent) is the subject of a Sept 2026 FEC complaint alleging coordination with his campaign; it is not reported as spending for him.
fec.history_note: First federal campaign; no earlier FEC candidacy found.

money2.note: As a donor: FEC records show 'a Dan Sullivan from Petersburg' gave $100 (Aug 2022) and $30 (Aug 2024) via ActBlue earmarked for Peltola's House campaigns (Alaska's News Source). That this donor is the candidate is likely but was not confirmed.

note.t: Senate candidate financial disclosure (required once a candidate passes $5,000) was not searched.

democracy.t: Wanted Sen. Sullivan to speak out against a Trump administration compensation fund that could benefit Jan. 6 rioters.
Calls Lt. Gov. Dahlstrom's voter-data decision 'profoundly wrong'; opposes Trump's pardons as unethical; supports ranked-choice voting.

note.t: Illinois native; Petersburg resident since 1980 by his account ('decades' per AP).

ballot.t: Filed May 29, 2026 as a Republican three days before the deadline, registered to vote as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom opened an investigation, citing 'credible allegations' of coordination; the NRSC demanded his removal. Elections Director Carol Beecher disqualified him (determination dated June 15) for not filing a 'good-faith' candidacy, citing his name use, his party switch at filing, a website resembling the senator's and his Democratic-linked consultant; she did not cite coordination evidence. Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews reversed on June 26, finding the standard had no legal basis, and the Alaska Supreme Court affirmed on June 29 and left the ballot listing to the division. He appears with no party label. After finishing third, he declined to withdraw by Aug 31, citing in part the removal of his Republican label.

complaints.t: Americans for Public Trust, a group with national Republican ties, filed an FEC complaint alleging that he and the 907 Initiative coordinated, producing excessive in-kind contributions, because his launch consultant Amber Lee sits on the 907 Initiative's board. Lee says she is an unpaid board member who does not direct its spending, and both say they followed the law. He declined comment.
complaints.status: Pending; the FEC lacks a quorum (two commissioners) to act. An allegation, not a finding.

checks.legal: Ballot litigation (he prevailed) documented through AP, Alaska Beacon and Alaska Public Media; CourtListener/Justia and Alaska CourtView not searched directly. News searches found no criminal or civil cases against him. A pending FEC complaint is recorded under 'complaints' (not a legal finding).
checks.foreign: None found in news; FARA and financial disclosure not searched.
checks.claims: Campaign website not opened. Bio sample = checkable claims in his Alaska Beacon voter-guide answers (4 rated). Campaign sample = his main public statements on his candidacy (filing rules, no coordination, branding) plus one checkable platform claim (Typhoon Halong reimbursement). No ads documented. Fewer than 10 issue claims exist in sources reached.
checks.democracy: Never held office; statements from AP and his Beacon questionnaire.

recordx.note: Not an officeholder. FEC committee RFAI/notices not checked. His statement of candidacy (FEC-1992084) is dated Jul 14, 2026, while committee coverage begins May 29.

gaps: Itemized FEC receipts/disbursements (who was paid; whether consultant was paid)
Independent confirmation of birthplace, 1980 arrival, Forest Service dates
research_notes: Thin record, as expected: no prior candidacy, no office, small FEC committee. Primary: 3,610 votes, 2.46% (unofficial Aug 25 printout); third place. The Alaska Current reports a post-election analysis found much of his vote came from Democratic-leaning areas, and the Beacon saw little sign of voter confusion. Party label: he filed as a Republican; the AP says he had no prior Republican affiliation, and the NRSC says his registration was 'undeclared.' Dates conflict across sources (disqualification June 10/12/15/16; Superior Court June 25/26). Using the AP's June 15 and June 26. The accusation that he is a Democratic plant comes from Sen. Sullivan's campaign and the NRSC; the documented facts are the consultant link and two small 2022/2024 donations to Peltola by a same-named Petersburg donor. He is not related to Sen. Dan S. Sullivan; nothing in Sen. Sullivan's record applies to him.
